newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBS SEEN WITH SLIGHT POSITIVE BIAS.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBS SEEN WITH SLIGHT POSITIVE BIAS.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to have a slight upward bias on Monday, supported by the dollar's sharp fall against the yen on Friday overseas, traders said.
"The market will be watching to see how the moves in the dollar against the yen affect the Tokyo stock market," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
JGBs will receive a boost if share prices fall due to the dollar's weakness, the trader said.
The Industrial Bank of Japan is due to announce its August long-term prime rate later on Monday.
Traders said the upside for September JGBs is likely to be limited due to an absence of investors during the summer holidays and a fall in U.S. Treasury bonds on Friday.

"Most domestic investors are on summer break, so moves in JGBs are likely to be limited. The dollar's fall against the yen may be a buy factor, but the sharp fall in Treasury bonds is a sell factor," a trader for a long-term credit bank's securities unit said.
The August long-term prime rate may be cut if the bond market rallies on Monday, the first trader said.
